newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Monday on a holiday mood ahead of the Chinese lunar new year, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,210 yuan ($386) per tonne, rising 60 yuan. It opened at 3,130 and hit a low of 3,122.
March fell 22 to 3,148, May rose 31 to 3,180, July rose 57 to 3,295, September fell eight to 3,290 and November dropped 14 to 3,346.
Combined volume fell to 53,100 tonnes from 53,500.
Traders said investors were reluctant to build large new positions with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
"Investor interest in trading has dropped, resulting in slower trade," one trader said. "The holiday mood will continue in the next few days."
Traders expect soybeans to continue to move in a narrow range before the 16-day holiday beginning February 1.
